combination.tip: Auto-tagged: this band is a combination (sum) mode, not a fundamental.

computational.tip: Assignment or frequency comes from a calculation (e.g. DFT), not a measured spectrum.

degenerated.tip: Two or more vibrational modes coincide at the same frequency and share one observed band.

direct-dosing.tip: Species generated by dosing/adsorbing its own desorbed counterpart directly (e.g. formate from formic acid), not via a genuine surface reaction.

drifts.tip: Measured by diffuse reflectance infrared spectroscopy (DRIFTS).

drifts-artifact.tip: Can be mistaken for a surface signal in DRIFTS but isn't (e.g. gas-phase absorption in the beam path).

fermi-resonance.tip: Auto-tagged: this band is one half of a Fermi-resonance doublet with another band.

frustrated-mode.tip: A free gas-phase rotation/translation that becomes a restoring-force vibration once the molecule is adsorbed.

ftir.tip: Measured by transmission FTIR rather than DRIFTS.

gas-phase.tip: Band belongs to a gas-phase species, not an adsorbed one.

hydride-marker.tip: Diagnostic marker band for a surface metal-hydride species.

ir-inactive.tip: Symmetry-forbidden in IR; included for context even though not directly observed.

isotopic-shift.tip: Assignment confirmed or supported by an isotope-substitution frequency shift.

misassignment-warning.tip: Position is a known trap for misassigning this band to a different species.

molecular-adsorption.tip: Species is adsorbed intact (not dissociated) rather than as a surface fragment.

overtone.tip: Band is an overtone of a lower fundamental, not the fundamental itself.

rotational-branches.tip: Auto-tagged: one rotational branch (P/Q/R) of a multi-branch transition; see its sibling branches.

site-sensitive.tip: Band position shifts meaningfully with adsorption site or surface composition.
